summary: Enterprise process automation, Frontend React role, design-system-driven AI-assisted UI development

motivation_letter.name: Goonja Gandhi
paragraphs: The most interesting phrase in Redwood's positioning is not 'automation' — it's 'single pane of glass.' When a platform is trusted to orchestrate mission-critical SAP and finance workflows, from job scheduling to record-to-report, simplicity is not a design preference; it is an operational necessity. That is why Redwood's move toward agentic orchestration matters: the more autonomous a system becomes, the more its interface has to show what is actually running, why it is running, and where human attention is required.

I studied linguistic philosophy before becoming an engineer, and it left me with a habit I still use: I ask what problem a concept is solving before I decide how to build with it. Enterprise frontend work rewards that habit. At TCS, leading a team of five developers on large Angular applications, I reduced API calls by 40% by designing state flow around the actual problem rather than the available pattern, and enforced WCAG standards until QA reported zero accessibility violations. Both were eventually about the same thing: making complex systems legible to the people depending on them.

I have been exploring the same boundary in my own work with AI systems. I built NewsAlign, a fact-verification platform using LangChain, FAISS, Hugging Face, and RAG pipelines; the central design insight was that retrieval and reasoning are different operations, and the interface had to make that distinction visible. An AI outcome you cannot inspect is not operational — it is just a claim. When I read Redwood's work on what it takes to make enterprise AI operational, that is exactly the question I recognized: models need orchestration, and orchestration needs transparency. A frontend developer who understands this distinction can help build interfaces where automation feels trustworthy rather than opaque.

I am not looking for a frontend role where the work stops at rendering. I want to build interfaces that carry complex systems without asking users to carry that complexity. That means taking performance seriously — I cut a large application's bundle from 941KB to under 300KB and raised its Lighthouse score from 73 to 95 — and it means treating accessibility as part of reliability. Redwood's platform sits in the middle of some of its customers' most critical processes. I would like to help make that platform clearer, faster, and easier to trust.
motivation_letter.closing: Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how I can contribute.

cover_letter.name: Goonja Gandhi
paragraphs: I am a frontend developer with five years of experience building React and TypeScript applications. I am open to relocating to the Netherlands, and I am drawn to Redwood Software because your shareable design system and AI-assisted development match my own focus on reusable UI and modern tooling.

At Tata Consultancy Services, I led a team of five developers while shaping frontend architecture. By introducing RxJS-based state management and caching strategies, I reduced API calls by 40% and improved application responsiveness. I also mentored junior developers and guided them through code reviews.

More recently, I built an AI-powered fact-checking platform with Next.js, LangChain, and RAG pipelines. This gave me hands-on experience with AI tools and performance work:
- Reduced bundle size from 941KB to under 300KB using code splitting and lazy loading.
- Raised Lighthouse performance from 73 to 95 through SSR and caching improvements.
- Achieved about 84% unit test coverage with Jest.

I also increased WCAG compliance by 30% in a React/Redux product while at Datapret, so accessibility is part of my definition of done. There, I collaborated with Agile teams and translated business needs into responsive interfaces. I have built real products with AI models and would enjoy focusing that experience on reviewing and optimizing AI-generated UI code within your design system.
cover_letter.closing: Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how I can contribute.
